content: The area of a semi-circle is calculated and then multiplied by the length of the plane and the average widths to determine the relevant dimensions. The bulkheads, which are located at the front and rear of the aircraft, are calculated as semi-circles based on the cabin width. The total surface area of the cargo holds (forward, aft, and bulk) in an aircraft is determined by converting the cargo hold volume into surface area. Volume capacity data can be found in tables of general aircraft characteristics. Each cargo hold volume must be calculated separately. All calculations are based solely on usable capacity. Characteristics such as water volume, if stated, should not be used for consistency. For aircraft with optional auxiliary fuel tanks that affect cargo hold volume, it is assumed that these tanks are not installed, and the maximum cargo volume is used. Some aircraft characteristics combine the total capacity of all holds. The section on loading combinations provides a breakdown of how loads are distributed within the holds. Freighters and double-decker commercial aircraft are calculated similarly to regular commercial aircraft, except that freighters lack linings, bulkheads, or overhead compartments, resulting in an area errata ratio of 1. For double-decker aircraft like the Boeing 747 and Airbus A380, the upper deck calculations must be added to the cabin floor area in square meters (upper deck cabin length × width). These aircraft have two levels of overhead lockers, but the bulkhead and lining areas are similar to those of standard commercial aircraft like the Boeing 737-800. An example calculation for the Boeing 737-800 can be sourced from the manufacturer’s website, which provides detailed aircraft characteristics. The volume of cargo in Boeing aircraft is calculated and documented in Boeing Aircraft Characteristics Documents. For example, the cargo volume for a specific model is 55.9 m³ (1585 ft³). For disinsection, a 2% emulsion of permethrin is prepared by mixing one part of a 50% EC formulation with 24 parts of water (42 mL of permethrin 50% EC per 1 L of water). The recommended application rate for cabin walls, ceilings, or cargo holds is 10 mL of permethrin per square meter. Residual spray amounts are calculated for effective treatment when mixed and applied correctly. For practical application, the floor is sprayed twice with a 10-mL solution (totaling 20 mL), with an additional 5 mL allocated for assumed drift from higher areas. Spray amounts for commercial passenger aircraft are calculated based on cabin and cargo hold dimensions, with specific liters per area provided for the entire aircraft. For freighter aircraft, spray amounts are similarly calculated, with specific liters per area provided for the entire aircraft. During disinsection, operators follow specific procedures to ensure thorough coverage. For example, operators move at a rate of one step or one row of seats per second, directing the spray towards open overhead lockers. In double-decker aircraft, the upper deck is treated separately, with operators ensuring all stowage compartments are open during treatment. The flight deck and internally accessed baggage storage areas are sprayed for specific durations (e.g., 2 seconds for the flight deck, 4 seconds for baggage areas). Cargo hold doors must be opened minimally to introduce the aerosol can and closed immediately after spraying to prevent spray from escaping. The aircraft must remain closed for 5 minutes after spraying before resuming air-conditioning and normal flight preparations. Separate external cargo holds are sprayed after all cargo and luggage have been loaded, with the amount specified in the relevant annex. The minimum aerosol spray amounts required for different aircraft types are specified, with detailed breakdowns for commercial passenger aircraft and freighters.
